GU GrÄtÄ UbartaitÄ, LRT.lt 2026.08.09 10:00 Vilnius TV Tower | J. StaceviÄius / LRT The Vilnius TV Tower, Lithuaniaâs tallest structure, is struck by lightning about 11 times more often than the surrounding area because of its height, location and lightning protection system, according to Lithuaniaâs meteorological service. The finding comes from a 2023 study cited by Gytis Valaika, chief communications specialist at the Lithuanian Hydrometeorological Service, after thunderstorms swept across the capital over the weekend, producing dramatic lightning displays and causing widespread damage. âThe tall tower acts as a giant lightning rod,â Valaika said about the 326-metre structure. âLightning always seeks the most conductive path to the ground. Because the tower stands on a hill, is very tall and has a grounding system, it is struck very frequently.â He said the tower also provides some protection to nearby areas by intercepting lightning that might otherwise strike surrounding locations, although it does not eliminate the risk entirely. Lightning | Shutterstock Valdas Kaminskas, communications director at Lithuaniaâs state-owned Radio and Television Centre, said the exact number of lightning strikes on the Vilnius TV Tower is not recorded, but the structure has been hit hundreds of times over the years. The tower was equipped with a lightning protection system during its construction. The system is designed to capture lightning strikes and safely channel the electrical discharge into the ground through lightning rods, which are regularly inspected, Kaminskas said. People inside the tower often do not notice when it is struck because the system directs the electrical current safely into the ground and prevents dangerous electromagnetic effects inside the building. TV Tower struck by lightning | Freeze frame Kaminskas said he was not aware of any cases in which employees or visitors had been injured by lightning strikes on the tower. âWe have no archival data on this, but I have never heard of any accidents involving tower staff or visitors caused by lightning,â he said. Beyond towers and other tall buildings, lightning in Lithuania also frequently strikes bodies of water such as rivers, lakes and springs, as well as tall trees, wind turbines and quarries, Valaika said. He added that comprehensive data on lightning strikes have only been collected since 2011 or 2012, making it too early to identify other statistically reliable lightning hotspots across the country. âWe need at least 20 to 30 years of observations to draw more reliable conclusions about the places lightning prefers or avoids,â he said. https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/a.text: ‘In rural France [on Mondays] 80% of businesses, restaurants and public bodies remain closed all day.’ Photograph: Pauline Cutler/Alamy View image in fullscreen ‘In rural France [on Mondays] 80% of businesses, restaurants and public bodies remain closed all day.’ Photograph: Pauline Cutler/Alamy Brief letters France Letters French Sunday and the Italian month off The antidote to a French Monday | August on holiday | School dinners | Dance-hall don’ts Mon 24 Aug 2026 13.32 EDT Last modified on Mon 24 Aug 2026 13.59 EDT Share As I write this, I’m enjoying my French Sunday ( Polly Hudson, 23 August ) with a croissant from the local bakery – open, of course – and a coffee. I’ll meet friends for lunch in a local riverside restaurant, then travel a few miles to a wonderful cafe, for even more coffee and their homemade cakes. Relaxing? Of course it is. It’s a much-needed antidote to a French Monday, particularly in rural France, where 80% of businesses, restaurants and public bodies remain closed all day in order to recover from the excesses of a “do nothing” Sunday. Roslyn Lockhart Montmorillon, France I enjoyed James Mackay’s article on villeggiatura , the Italian tradition of taking August off, which is shown to help rather than hinder economic output ( 17 August ). As he says, though, the point is “reclaiming life from the totalising logic of the market”. For an expansion of this idea, I recommend the work of Amintore Fanfani, Luigino Bruni and Stefano Zamagni, who deserve to be better known in Britain. Like Pope Leo, they put human dignity and flourishing at the centre of economics. Catherine McLoughlin London Many problems have an easy solution that is wrong, but I suspect that including food standards in Ofsted results would fix this one very fast ( Most English secondary schools are breaking healthy food rules, finds report, 24 August ). Brian Fish Leeds In Elgin in the 1960s, if you were caught snogging in the Two Red Shoes dance hall, a spotlight would be shone on you to kill the moment ( Letters, 20 August ). https://www.dw.com/en/ukraine-s-zelensky.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5OmfA Zelenskyy is concerned that Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin could divide up global spheres of influence between them Image: Dmitri Lovetsky/AP Photo/picture alliance Advertisement Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has warned that a planned meeting between Russia , China and the United States next month could present the three participants with an opportunity to redraw global spheres of influence. "We really don't want this to turn into 'Yalta 2, 3, 4' with a redistribution of influence," he said in comments to journalists on Wednesday, referring to the 1945 Yalta Conference in Crimea , where Allied powers redrew the world map in the wake of the Second World War . Putin raised idea of three-way summit with Trump: What to know The Kremlin has previously indicated that preparations were underway for a meeting between Russian President Vladimir Putin and his US and Chinese counterparts, Donald Trump and Xi Jinping , on the sidelines of an Asia-Pacific summit next month. The Wall Street Journal first broke the news about the three-way summit earlier this month and said that Trump had not agreed to attend the summit at the time. But the Journal said Trump was open to the proposal — that had been raised by Putin — since he wanted to bring an end to the war in Ukraine. "What China, Russia and the United States might discuss has not yet been clearly defined," Zelenskyy said, adding that "Russia wants this meeting more than anyone," warning against handing Moscow "another major diplomatic advantage." For years now, Russia has been seeking a new agreement with Washington on European security architecture, and in particular an end to what Putin considers NATO's aggressive expansion towards Russia. Putin has falsely repeatedly said Ukraine war was an act of self-defense Putin continues to cast the ongoing invasion of Ukraine as a response to such a NATO threat – a position widely rejected in Kyiv and the rest of Europe. Zelenskyy's warning came ahead of planned talks between Ukrainian, Russian and US envoys in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) next month. No specific date has been set for the Abu Dhabi meeting, but Kyiv is keen for it to take place before the potential Russia-China-US summit. Before that, it was also confirmed on Wednesday that Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov will travel to the United States for a meeting with G20 counterparts in Atlanta on October 30-31. Zelenskyy's comments were released as he traveled to the Netherlands for talks with Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jetten Image: Remko de Waal/ANP/picture alliance Zelenskyy in Netherlands Zelenskyy's remarks were released as he traveled to the Netherlands for meetings with Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jetten and Dutch King Willem-Alexander in The Hague. The Dutch government said on Wednesday it would provide Ukraine with €1.2 billion ($1.3 billion) in non-military support over the next ⁠years. Zelenskyy also held a phone call with British Prime Minister Andy Burnham to thank him for an ​extra £10 ⁠billion ($13.29 billion/€11.94 billion) of support announced earlier ⁠on ​Wednesday. "A truly ​strong very timely step coming right Russia needs to and ​feel that Ukraine will not be left ​alone to deal with the problems ⁠Russia ​is so ​eager to escalate," he wrote on social media. But Ukraine's greatest assets in its defense against Russian aggression remain US Patriot air defense missiles, and Zelenskyy urged Washington to increase supplies. Zelenskyy said Ukraine had been receiving 12 missiles a month this year but is being targeted with "150 ballistic missiles a month." Oleshky truce holding for now, Zelenskyy says Meanwhile on the battlefield, officials said a six-day ceasefire in a Russian-occupied town in southern Ukraine held for its first day and night. The localized truce in the devastated town of Oleshky began on Tuesday and is due to last until Sunday, enabling a planned humanitarian operation to provide around 2,000 remaining residents with urgently needed food and medicine , and evacuate those who want to leave. "We are grateful that they are organizing this possibility to evacuate people," said President Zelenskyy. The plight of Oleshky in Ukraine's southern Kherson region caught the attention of US first lady Melania Trump, who the White House said helped broker the humanitarian mission . If the ceasefire holds, it will be the first time in more than four-and-a-half years of fighting that both sides have observed a significant truce, with previous attempts quickly unraveling. "This is the biggest de-escalation since 2022," said Ukraine's negotiator, Davyd ‌Arakhamia, on Tuesday, adding every step brings peace closer. Oleshky ceasefire comes into effect in Ukraine war To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video Drone attacks in Kharkiv, Belgorod — and off Bulgaria Elsewhere, however, the war raged on with five people, including a four-year-old child, injured in a Russian drone strike on the northeastern Ukrainian city of Kharkiv overnight. In Moscow, the Russian Defense Ministry said air defenses had downed 531 Ukrainian drones on Tuesday night and into Wednesday morning, but local authorities in the Belgorod border region said one person was killed in a drone attack. And in Sofia, Bulgarian Defense Minister Dimitar Stoyanov said three maritime drones struck a container ship in the Black Sea off the coast of Bulgaria . The crew evacuated the vessel and there were no immediate reports of casualties, according to Bulgarian state news agency BTA, but the incident took place as defense ministers from Bulgaria, Romania and Turkey were meeting in Sofia for trilateral talks focused on Black Sea security. "We follow with concern the intense attacks on commercial vessels in the Black Sea ​and call on the sides to act with common sense, in line with the principle of navigational safety in open seas," said Turkish Defense Minister Yasar Guler. "The necessary warnings are constantly being conveyed to both sides to keep commercial navigational out of the conflict zone and ​immediately halt attacks on civilian vessels." A series of drone attacks have occurred this month off the coasts of NATO members Romania and Bulgaria. Russia has not taken responsibility, but suspicion has increasingly fallen on Moscow. "The logic points in that direction," Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev told parliament earlier this month. "The problem is that we cannot prove it."
